data.name: Barraq
data.gender_notes: Barraq is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘Al Barr’, meaning ‘the thunder’. It symbolizes power, strength, and the awe-inspiring might of Allah’s creations. The name Barraq carries the meaning “Thunder” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Barraq usually hope their child will grow to embody thunder and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name inspired by Allah’s power and majesty.
data.etymology: Barraq belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Thunder.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Barraq total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: براق
in_arabic.meaning: براق هو اسم يعني اللامع أو شديد اللمعان في اللغة العربية
in_arabic.long_meaning: براق هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و يعني اللامع أو شديد اللمعان. وقد ورد هذا الاسم في القرآن الكريم في سورة النجم: 'وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالْأُفُقِ الْمُبِينِ * وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ' (النجم: 18-19). وبراق هو اسم من أسماء النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، كما ورد في الحديث النبوي: 'أُعطيتُ خمسًا: أُعطيتُ الرِّشَالَ، وَأُعطيتُ المَشُورَةَ، وَأُعطيتُ بَراقًا وهو الذي حمله من مكة إلى المدينة'.

in_urdu.name: براق
in_urdu.meaning: براق کا مطلب ہے چمکدار یا بہت زیادہ چمکدار
in_urdu.long_meaning: براق ایک مذکر اسم ہے جس کی اصل عربی ہے۔ یہ نام چمکدار یا بہت زیادہ چمکدار کے معنی میں ہے۔ عربی میں اس کا تلفظ 'براق' ہے جو قرآن مجید میں بھی ذکر ہوا ہے۔ براق نبی کریم صلی اللہ علیہ و آلہ و سلم کا بھی ایک نام ہے، جس کا ذکر حدیث مبارکہ میں آیا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: बराक़
in_hindi.meaning: बराक़ का अर्थ है चमकदार या अत्यधिक चमकदार
in_hindi.long_meaning: बराक़ एक पुल्लिंग नाम है जिसकी उत्पत्ति अरबी भाषा से हुई है। यह नाम चमकदार या अत्यधिक चमकदार के अर्थ में है। अरबी भाषा में इसका उच्चारण 'बराक़' है जो कुरआन में भी उल्लेखित है। बराक़ पैगंबर मुहम्मद सल्लल्लाहु अलैहि वसल्लम का भी एक नाम है, जिसका उल्लेख हदीस में आया है।

in_pashto.name: براق
in_pashto.meaning: براق د لامع یا ډیر لامع معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: براق یو مذکر نوم دی چی د عربي اصلي څخه يی اخیستل شوی دی. دا نوم د لامع یا ډیر لامع په معنی دی. په عربي کي يی تلفظ 'براق' دی چی په قرآن کريم کي يی ذکر شوی دی. براق د نبي کريم صلی الله عليه وسلم يو نوم دی، چی په حدیث کښی يی ذکر شوی دی.

in_english.name: Barraq
in_english.long_meaning: Barraq is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, meaning 'shining,' 'brilliant,' or 'radiant.' Etymologically derived from the Arabic root 'B-R-Q,' which conveys the notion of brightness or luminosity. In Islamic tradition, Barraq is one of the names attributed to the Prophet Muhammad, as mentioned in hadith. The name signifies illumination, spiritual guidance, and enlightenment. Historically, Barraq has been used across various Muslim cultures, symbolizing positive attributes such as brilliance and enlightenment.

The name holds immense significance in a culture that reveres the beauty and majesty of nature and understands it as a manifestation of Allah’s power.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hakam's 'Futuh al-Sham' - The Conquest of Syria The name Barraq carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Barraq ibn Marwan was a chief of the Banu Kalb tribe who betrayed the Arab Muslim army during the Battle of Marj al-Saffar in 634 AD by killing Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab's top commander Al-Ala' ibn al-Hadrami. This event is recounted in detail in Ibn Abd al-Hakam's historical work, where Barraq is also described as the father of the future Umayyad Caliph Muawiya I.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri's 'Ansab al-Ashraf' - The Genealogies of Noble Arab Tribes The name Barraq carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Barraq ibn Marwan is mentioned in al-Baladhuri's historical work as a chief of the Kalb tribe who supported the Umayyad Dynasty and played a significant role in the Battle of Nahr al-Kabir in 750 AD. The battle was a pivotal moment in Islamic history, as it ended the Umayyad rule and installed the Abbasid Caliphate. Barraq's loyalty to the Umayyads is highlighted in this reference.
